digest.component_or_area: rich-text codec cutover and echo suppression
propositions: State-based echo suppression compares current Jira value against last-synced baseline to prevent re-emitting unchanged rich-text content, using normalized local and decoded remote paths that differ in application.

Two distinct compares are required: emit-path compares normalized fit-outbound local against decoded-inbound remote; baseline-path compares normalized local against decoded baseline wire, both normalized via RichTextCodec.normalize_outbound.

A change-gated 8-byte rich_sha digest stored inline in the binding increments a rich_reemit counter on re-emission of the same wire; at threshold 2, one post-push GET reads back the remote value to advance the baseline, then subsequent passes suppress the echo.

WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound must be redefined as decode_inbound(to_wire(value)) to restore the codec law; all three DC send sites must route through to_wire (render markdown to wiki) before fit_outbound to avoid shipping un-rendered markdown.
Concurrent both-sides edits on description keep rebar-originated local value (local-wins per a713) while raising an outbound-field-conflict alert with the remote value recorded.

The cutover is flag-gated by reconciler.rich_text_cutover config (off/cloud/dc/both, defaults off) and degrades to plain-text ADF when marklas optional extra is absent, with no error or half-converted wire.
